00001| /**
00002|  * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
00003|  *
00004|  * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
00005|  * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
00006|  * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
00007|  * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
00008|  * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
00009|  *
00010|  * Dual mode:
00011|  *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
00012|  *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
00013|  *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
00014|  *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
00015|  *
00016|  * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
00017|  * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
00018|  */
00019| 
00020| import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
00021| import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
00022| import { dirname } from 'node:path';
00023| import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
00024| 
00025| /**
00026|  * Build the OpenCode CLI argument list.
00027|  *
00028|  *   - `run <prompt> --format json` is always emitted (`--format json` gives the
00029|  *     structured JSON event stream we parse for the transcript).
00030|  *   - `--model <extra.cliModel>` is appended when a model override is present.
00031|  *     cliModel is HOST-computed (resolveOpenCodeModel in agent.ts, threaded via
00032|  *     runnerExtra like codex's resolved model) so a canonical gateway id like
00033|  *     `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` arrives as `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` —
00034|  *     the form OpenCode routes through the configured `vercel` provider. There is
00035|  *     deliberately NO fallback to input.model: passing it verbatim is the exact
00036|  *     mis-route this fixes, and both runner entry points (the orchestrator and
00037|  *     the judge's eval-helper) always ship extra.
00038|  *   - else, when modelPolicy === 'native-default', `--print-logs --log-level INFO`
00039|  *     is appended so older OpenCode versions print the CLI-selected model (the
00040|  *     log-scrape path) without a follow-up export call.
00041|  *
00042|  * @param {{prompt:string, modelPolicy?:string, extra?:Record<string,unknown>}} input
00043|  * @returns {string[]}
00044|  */
00045| export function buildOpenCodeCliArgs(input) {
00046|   const cliArgs = ['run', input.prompt, '--format', 'json'];
00047|   const cliModel = input.extra?.cliModel;
00048|   if (cliModel) {
00049|     cliArgs.push('--model', String(cliModel));
00050|   } else if (input.modelPolicy === 'native-default') {
00051|     cliArgs.push('--print-logs', '--log-level', 'INFO');
00052|   }
00053|   return cliArgs;
00054| }
00055| 
00056| /**
00057|  * Report the observed model in the caller's namespace.
00058|  *
00059|  * When the host prefixed the requested model with `vercel/` (extra.cliModel !==
00060|  * input.model), OpenCode observes it back in its own provider namespace —
00061|  * `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` for a requested `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`.
00062|  * Un-apply exactly that translation so observed === requested holds for callers
00063|  * that speak canonical gateway ids, and a gateway substitution still surfaces as
00064|  * a clean gateway id (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4`, not `vercel/anthropic/...`).
00065|  *
00066|  * Everything else passes through untouched: native-default runs (no override —
00067|  * consumers already treat `vercel/google/gemini-3-pro-preview` as canonical),
00068|  * callers that already speak OpenCode's namespace (`vercel/...` requested), and
00069|  * extraProviders runs (their providerID isn't `vercel`).
00070|  *
00071|  * @param {string|undefined} observedModel
00072|  * @param {{model?:string, extra?:Record<string,unknown>}} input
00073|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00074|  */
00075| export function normalizeObservedModel(observedModel, input) {
00076|   if (!observedModel) {
00077|     return observedModel;
00078|   }
00079|   const cliModel = input.extra?.cliModel;
00080|   const hostPrefixed = typeof cliModel === 'string' && cliModel !== input.model;
00081|   if (hostPrefixed && observedModel.startsWith('vercel/')) {
00082|     return observedModel.slice('vercel/'.length);
00083|   }
00084|   return observedModel;
00085| }

/**

 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.

 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.

 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be

title: Migrating to Cache Components
nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components
description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation

---

When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).

The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.

title: Migrating to Cache Components
nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components
description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/getting-started/caching
    - app/guides/preserving-ui-state
    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
    - app/guides/authentication-with-cache-components
    - app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
---

When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).

The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.

title: use cache
description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

> **Good to know:**
>

title: use cache
description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

> **Good to know:**

The `cacheLife` function is used to set the cache lifetime of a function or component. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component.

## Usage

### Basic setup

To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:

events.content:
Done. Migrated the publishing app to Cache Components on the `cache-components` branch, and the production build passes with no routes opted out.

**Changes:**
- `next.config.ts` — replaced the legacy `experimental.dynamicIO` flag with `cacheComponents: true`.
- `app/news/page.tsx` — removed `export const revalidate = 3600`; moved the feed fetch into a `use cache` function with `cacheLife('hours')`, preserving the hourly refresh policy (build confirms `Revalidate 1h`).
- `app/preview/page.tsx` — removed `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` (not needed; pages are dynamic by default) and wrapped the `cookies()` read in a `<Suspense>`-boundary child component so the static shell prerenders and the request-specific draft streams in per request.

**Build result** — all routes prerendered, none opted out (`instant` appears nowhere in the tree):

| Route | Mode |
|---|---|
| `/` | Static |
| `/news` | Static, revalidate 1h / expire 1d |
| `/preview` | Partial Prerender (static shell + dynamic draft) |

The preview route is correctly request-specific (◐ PPR with the cookie-driven draft streaming at request time), and the newsroom keeps its hourly ISR. TypeScript is clean.
